title: Five minutes to the first picture
question: On hazelgrove/hazel#2597, the full livelits branch, the Livelit Playground's Scenes slide has taken about five minutes to draw its first picture, and the Witch slide almost three; #2635 draws both in about 12 seconds. ^report(4) put this down to #2597 lacking the speedups of #2469 (modular editors). Is it really that long, and why? And a fix, tried.

builds.note: dev build, served locally; measured on the evening of 2026-10-12
dev build, served locally; has all of #2469, so both c07bdacead and a05f8e5791

builds.name: 2597 with c07bdacead
builds.commit: 1fa1384445 plus c07bdacead (from #2469, by Andrew Blinn), as local commit 0f64f97a10
builds.note: local branch perf/2597-stream-throttle, not pushed; two small conflicts, resolved as #experiment describes

builds.name: 2597 with the port (What next, step 1)
builds.note: c07bdacead on #2597 itself, later on 2026-10-12, with the same resolution

builds.name: 2597, earlier on 2026-10-12
builds.note: the first four rows of the table under #really, from #2609's findings 25 and 28 and ^report(4): before and after the worker's slices ran back to back, after the view's casts were fixed, and with all three of the day's view fixes

runtime: headless Firefox over WebDriver (the report states no version), a fresh profile per run, dev builds served locally; one run at a time, on one laptop
runs: Each run cold: the slide opened at /fresh in a fresh profile, so nothing saved was read. Printed per run: #2597 at 1fa1384445, one time per slide; #2635, three times on Scenes and one on Witch; the copy with c07bdacead, three times per slide; #2597 at a15c6f0b65, two on Scenes and one on Witch. Profiles: one load each of #2597 (sampled every 4 ms) and of the copy (every 1 ms), started before navigation and saved a few seconds after the first picture.

measures.first picture: s: the time since navigation when an svg with more than 40 shapes first appeared, recorded in the page by a MutationObserver, 'so the time is exact even while the page is too busy to answer the test script'
measures.messages: count: the page's message events from the worker, during the whole load (2,520 on #2597, 86 on the copy)
measures.main thread busy: s, profiled: the page's main thread over the whole load, from opening the slide until its first picture (353 s on #2597, 97% of it the app's update loop; on the copy, the app's code about 31 s)
measures.per message: ms, profiled: the page's work per message from the worker, about 140 ms on #2597; receiving all 2,520 took 0.5 s
measures.worker idle: %: of the load, the eval worker idle: 98.7% on #2597
measures.Share of the main thread: %: of the samples of the page's main thread during #2597's load; an indented ('of which') row is part of the row above it

times: the page's MutationObserver timestamps, since navigation. Profiled times run long: under the profiler the first picture came at 348 s on #2597 and 29.5 s on the copy, against 287.5 and about 17 s without it.

figures.17.4 s: the same, with c07bdacead (median of three: 17.6, 16.6, 17.4 s)
figures.12.5 s: #2635, which has all of #2469 (median of three: 11.4, 13.2, 12.5 s)
figures.2,520 -> 86: worker messages the page handled while opening Scenes, #2597 and the copy with c07bdacead

cited.what: c07bdacead on a generated 1,000-item program: the stream messages after the slide was drawn, and the main thread's work after opening it
a05f8e5791's interval growing with the program, 100 ms up to 1 s, on a 2,000-item program
a Kids' Choice slider release on #2597 and #2635, and #2597's whole-program statics in it (the other #2597 slowness, not addressed here)
the size of the worker's evaluation slices, after each of which it can send partial results (a code fact)

provenance: No raw file was kept with this report: the WebDriver driver's output and both Gecko profiles were not saved with it. Every number here exists only as printed in the report.
